root_cause: The objective planner never asks whether a unit's OC changes who controls the objective it is committed to. Three different code paths do this, one per finding. (s7475 r3 P1) Pass 1 hold: on a held_threatened objective EVERY movable holder holds ('holding under threat'), whatever the margin. KEEP-OC's locked-OC release sits in a later elif and never runs for held_threatened. Custodian Guard Beta (9 OC in range) stayed on a centre held 20 vs 9 while the enemy-held obj_nml_1 (8 OC) went uncontested. COORD-5 projected 7 more enemy OC, but all of it came from enemy units locked in combat with ours. B gained by denial: the opponent's per_objective primary fell from 6 to 3 (round 3) and 15 to 12 (round 4) in the A/B records, with our own Death Trap VP the same. (s7478 r3 P2) OBJ-ASSIGN-1 swapped Custodian Guard Beta (OC 9) onto the uncontrolled, UNCONTESTED obj_home_2 in place of the Prosecutors (OC 8). Both arrive in 2 phases; the swap bought only 4" of spare movement that nobody races for. The Prosecutors then went to the contested centre and Beta's OC was spent where 1 OC captures. (s7463 r1 P2, drift) The base now sends Kommandos to the PASS-3 support fallback: obj_center's need of 6 is filled by two Battlewagons on a 3-turn race, and LONE-TRIP filters the centre out of the Kommandos' support options. So _find_best_remaining_objective reinforces obj_nml_2, held 18 vs 0, where its OC changes nothing.
fix_summary: FIX_MARGINAL_OC (default 1; 0 restores base exactly). Two narrow parts. (a) MOC-HOLD, pass 1: a movable holder of a held_threatened objective with no remaining need is freed when two things hold. First, the OC left without it beats the threat by MARGINAL_OC_HOLD_MARGIN=2. Left OC = friendly_oc minus its in-range OC (MissionManager predicate) minus holders already freed there. Threat = enemy OC in range now PLUS enemy OC that can walk in next move (COORD-5 reach, units engaged with ours left out). Second, it has a candidate of at most MARGINAL_OC_MAX_TURNS=2 turns, not a lost race, arriving before round 5 ends, to an objective we do not control that still needs OC. Pass 2 then assigns it normally (LONE-TRIP/RACE-SKIP still apply). The threat is the SUM of now and next-move OC, not KEEP-OC's max, to protect the held objective in later rounds. Freed holders are tallied, so two holders cannot both leave on the same surplus. (b) MOC-SWAP, OBJ-ASSIGN-1: no swap of a higher-OC unit onto an uncontrolled objective with no enemy OC in range or one move away, when both units arrive in the same Movement phase (only spare inches differ). Logs: [MARGINAL_OC] MOC-HOLD / MOC-SWAP when a decision changes; untagged 'MOC-CHECK' debug line per held_threatened holder checked.

Guardrail replays (5 positions, both players, to end of next round): 0 in each. Bench mirror_custodes_2000_postdeploy, seed 93101, both seat orders: 0 and 0 [MARGINAL_OC] lines; both games ended -53 with identical margins. A second identical pair that also kept near-miss lines showed 9 MOC-CHECK evaluations in one game (margins -18 to +7; the +7 case, Prosecutors on obj_home_1, had no open objective within 2 turns) and 6 OBJ-ASSIGN-1 swaps per game, none same-phase onto an uncontested objective.
risks: BENCH REACH IS ZERO: neither part fired in a full Custodes-mirror game pair (seed 93101), so the bench cannot measure this design as it stands; the gain rests on the two decision checks. Rounds 3-5: MOC-HOLD leaves an objective held by a margin of at least 2 OC against everything in range plus every free enemy unit one move away. The holders left behind can still be shot or fought off it in the enemy turn. The engaged-enemy exclusion is the riskiest part: an engaged enemy unit can Fall Back and end within range, or the unit it is engaged with can be destroyed in the fight phase, which frees the enemy to walk on next turn. In round 5 a 2-turn target is cut by the arrive-before-game-end test, so only 1-turn flips release a holder late. That trades a safe hold for a flip that scores at once, and the trade is wrong when the remaining holders die. Secondary cards: freeing a holder sends a unit forward onto an enemy-held objective, which helps spread cards (Engage on All Fronts, Behind Enemy Lines, A Tempting Target / no-man's-land cards) and denial. Centre-type cards (Centre Ground) keep their units, because the remaining OC must still beat the threat. Unlike round 2's FAR-TRIP/OVERCOMMIT, nothing here holds a unit back or shortens a trip; it can only send a unit forward from a surplus. MOC-SWAP: the cheaper/lower-OC unit takes the empty objective and the higher-OC unit goes to a contested one. Risk: a contested trip is more dangerous for the elite unit, but LONE-TRIP and RACE-SKIP still filter it, and the swap is kept whenever the faster unit arrives a phase sooner. Not addressed: finding s7463 (pass-3 support reinforcing a held_safe objective with surplus OC), because fixing it means overriding LONE-TRIP, which guardrail s7468 shows is harmful.
